title: finding(app-shell): ai:input carries a curated BLOCK_CONFIG panel but is neither a palette block, a spec PageComponentType, nor a rendered type
body:
Ruled: 5810020464 · letter remove (delete the ai:input config panel; close the test exemption) · 2026-09-24T07:48Z

Found by the census objectui#8216 asked for (branch `claude/issue-8216-block-config-schema-parity`). Filed unassigned, out of that card's scope. Measured on `origin/main` `f20e57d62`, installed `@objectstack/spec` `17.2.0`.

## What

`BLOCK_CONFIG['ai:input']` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/block-config.ts:534`) curates two controls, `agentName` and `placeholder`, with translations in both locale tables (`metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, en at `:737`-`:739`, zh at `:2634`-`:2636`). Measured against every face that could make that block authorable:

- **Not in the palette.** `ai:input` is not a `BlockTypeId` and has no `BLOCK_TYPE_META` row (`previews/block-types.ts`) — only `ai:suggestion` is offered in the `ai` category. It is not in `PALETTE_EXCLUSIONS` either, so it carries no exclusion decision.
- **Not a spec block type.** `PageComponentType` has 34 members and `ai:input` is not one; `ComponentPropsMap` has 42 keys and does not carry it. So no page document containing it is spec-valid, and there is no props shape to judge its two keys against.
- **No real renderer.** It appears only in `PROTOCOL_COMPONENTS` (`packages/components/src/renderers/placeholders.tsx:102`) — the opt-in placeholder list that only `apps/console` bootstraps via `registerPlaceholders`. It is deliberately NOT in `PALETTE_PLACEHOLDER_BLOCKS`, the narrow set registered eagerly for blocks the palette offers. `packages/cli/src/utils/known-schema-types.ts:360` records it as `protocol-placeholder:ai:input`.

## Why this is worth a card

This is the `ai:chat_window` shape objectui#2943 already dealt with once, minus the palette entry. The repo's own rule is written into `block-config.ts` at the `ai` section: "No `ai:chat_window` panel: the block is not in the palette … A config panel for an unauthorable block is how the contradiction stayed invisible." `ai:input` has that panel.

The `block-config.test.ts` case that would have caught it exempts itself here by construction — "a block with a config panel is a block the palette offers" filters to `specNames.includes(t)`, and `ai:input` is not a spec name, so it is skipped as a "palette-native objectui block". It is not palette-native: `object-grid` and `grid` really are offered, and `ai:input` is not.

⚠️ Grading is triage's, and the honest read is narrow: nobody can reach this panel from the palette today, so the cost is curated surface plus four translation entries that outlived their block, not a broken author flow. It is the same category as the exclusion-reason truthfulness the repo already pins (`__tests__/exclusion-reason-truthfulness.test.ts`) — a decision record that says something untrue about the tree.

## The decision this needs

One of two, and they are genuinely different:

- **Remove** the panel and its four i18n entries — the enforce-or-remove default under the startup-focus rule, matching `ai:chat_window`'s treatment. This is the recommendation.
- **Keep it and make the block real** — a `BLOCK_TYPE_META` row plus a renderer plus an upstream `PageComponentType` member. That is a capability expansion with no measured pull and should not happen on this card's evidence.
